post.description: Only where the binding can take one (ORDER_REVISION). Sent under a key built from the notice, so a repeat is the same send. The body names the revision of the notice the operator saw: 409 STALE_VERSION, with nothing sent and nothing closed, when the order has been weighed again since. Otherwise answers 200 with the outcome in the body: a refusal, an unreachable till, an unknown outcome and a notice that moved while the till was being asked (SUPERSEDED) are ordinary answers, and in each the notice stays open with a stable failure code.

get.description: The picker behind the drawer's «attach». Read under the case's own capability, because the order-remedy console's read needs a tenant-scope payment capability a branch case worker does not hold. Conversion is a lower bound: a provenance written after its day closed is counted by a rebuild, not by the close. A null count means the row was closed before the measure existed (not measured), which is never zero. talkDurationSeconds is the call's length, first event to end, ring and queue time included; the name is historic.

post.description: orders.md §5: the New order screen's Создать. Reuses the ordinary checkout path end to end — the same cart, quote and payment rules a customer's own checkout takes — so this is never a second order-creation path to keep in step with pricing, inventory or payment. What differs is attribution alone: `customerAccountId` is the resolved or freshly created customer (`POST /customers` and `POST .../customer-lookups` beside this endpoint resolve it), and the order records the operator as its created_by_actor (V0029) rather than the customer. `paymentMethodCode` is checked against the operator channel's own payment matrix, not hard-coded to cash (row 1.3e). `fulfillmentMode` may be DELIVERY, using a saved address of the resolved customer's own (row 1.3b/1.3c). `requestedFor` (row 1.3d) asks for a promise time instead of now; a branch closed at that time refuses with BRANCH_CLOSED_AT_REQUESTED_TIME_CONFIRM until `overrideOutOfHours` is resubmitted true, or with BRANCH_CLOSED_AT_REQUESTED_TIME outright when the branch's own policy refuses a pre-order into that slot at all. On success, route straight to GET .../orders/{orderId}: the operator is still on the phone and needs to read the number back.
post.summary: Take an order by phone

post.description: orders.md §5, gap map row 1.3g (ADR 0040). For when an aggregator's own integration is down and they call the branch instead: the order is recorded under that aggregator's own AGGREGATOR-system-type channel with the total it already collected, never run back through the HorecaOS quote pipeline — `pricing_authority = EXTERNAL`, `entry_mode = MANUAL`, and `origin`/`marketplace_binding_id` set exactly as an automated partner push sets them, so this order counts in the channel mix as what it is rather than as an ordinary own-channel sale. Creates no customer account: a marketplace order never matches one (ADR 0040). `fulfillmentMode` DELIVERY (wave 11 w5-fulfillment-destination) reuses the New order screen's own structured destination — one of the named customer's saved addresses, never a second, untyped address path — and opens a delivery plan the same way a native order's confirmation does; PICKUP is unchanged and carries neither `customerAccountId` nor `destination`.
post.summary: Record an order an aggregator phoned through by hand

get.description: orders.md §2.4 (ADR 0102): the board's filter set, every predicate applied in the database rather than in the browser. An empty status filter returns everything rather than silently hiding the closed ones, because a branch reconciling a shift needs the orders that are over as much as the ones that are live. `reference` narrows this branch's orders by the order's own number or by an aggregator's or a POS's identifier (ADR 0040), normalised so `0911-142`, `0911 142` and `#0911142` are one query — it is a filter, not the tenant-wide search of orders.md §2.8, which needs an endpoint at its own scope: nothing here reaches past this location. It is not a phone lookup either: a phone number goes in a POST body, never a query string (orders.md §2.8, ADR 0029). `origin` narrows to how the order arrived — `HORECAOS` for the tenant's own channels or `MARKETPLACE` for anything recorded under an aggregator's own binding (ADR 0040, wave 9 row `1.1c`) — the coarse «Источник» toggle orders.md §2.4 names; `marketplaceBindingId` picks one specific aggregator binding when a tenant runs several (the options are `GET .../orders/marketplace-bindings`). `paymentStatus` narrows to `ordering.orders.payment_status_projection` (V0022, gap map row 1.1c) — Оплата, never to be confused with `paymentMethodCode`'s Способ оплаты. The four secondary toggles of orders.md §2.4: `late` (Только опаздывающие — not over and past the promise plus the branch's `ordering.lateness` grace, ADR 0030), `problem` (С проблемой — a process needing an operator or failed and awaiting retry), `callbackRequested` (Требуется звонок — the flag the callback amendment raises and clears) and `fiscalStatus` (Фискализация — any fiscal document of the order in one of the given statuses, ADR 0038). `include` names the optional facts the board's picker columns draw (`courierEta`, `source`, `fiscal`, `distance`, `externalNumber`), each read in one batch for the page and only when asked for; the payment method and the item summary are always on the row. Keyset-paginated (ADR 0031): pass the previous page's `nextCursor` back as `cursor`. Changing a filter invalidates the cursor — start the list again — because a window cut for one filter set says nothing about another. The same board across a brand's branches is `GET /api/v1/operations/tenants/{t}/brands/{b}/orders/board`, which needs `ORDER_READ` at BRAND scope.
get.summary: The order board: the branch's orders, filtered and paged

post.description: Gap map rows 1.3 and 0.1c. DELIVERY ranks every branch of this brand with a live ADR 0037 zone covering `point` by that zone's own priority/area order — the identical order DeliveryFeeResolver would apply if checkout later priced this address at that branch, never a second ranking rule. PICKUP has no address to rank a zone against, so every open branch of the brand is a candidate, ranked by current load ascending. Every candidate carries its ADR 0036 open/closed state, preparation band, and the exact brand-scoped live order count the branch leaderboard (row 0.1c) already reads once per tick — closed branches are included, not filtered out, so an operator can see the resolver's own top pick is closed rather than have it silently vanish. `proposedLocationId` is the first open candidate in ranked order, or the top-ranked one if none is open. Authorized at this request's own `locationId` (the operator's current branch) with ORDER_READ — the same read LOCATION_STAFF already holds for this screen — even though the candidates it returns span the whole brand: this is the explicit, human-facing search DeliveryFeeResolver's own doc names as the correct home for this question, never a second zone algorithm.

post.description: ADR 0039. N independent commands under one bulk operation id, never one all-or-nothing transaction: each order is applied through the same single-order service a lone request would use, in its own transaction, so one already-settled order cannot fail the other hundred and ninety-nine. Always 202 with a per-item outcome list, capped at 200 orders. ADVANCE targets PREPARING, READY or FULFILLING only; CANCEL names a reason from GET .../reject-reasons' sibling, the tenant's outcome-reason registry, exactly like a single cancellation. A resubmission carrying the same Idempotency-Key changes nothing and returns the outcome already recorded, applied or failed alike — a re-run does not retry the failures. ASSIGN_COURIER (ADR 0172) names one courierId and a reasonCode, assigns each selected delivery order to that courier in submission order up to the courier type's ceiling, and additionally requires delivery.manual_assign: holding order.bulk-action alone answers 403 for the request. Problem codes are stable per item; a person's assignment overrides a dispatch rule and says so in the item's note. Never creates a run.
post.summary: Apply ADVANCE, CANCEL or ASSIGN_COURIER to an operator's own order selection

get.description: orders.md §2.3: each tab shows a live count computed before the tab's own filters apply, and until ADR 0045's COUNTERS signal exists this is what computes them. One aggregate over the location's orders, scoped identically to the list above. Внимание's live severity queue (late orders, stuck processes) is not among these — it is derived per render from the promise and the clock, never stored, so a count of it would be wrong five seconds after being cached. Two independent ways to name a period, never both at once: `from`/`to` are the order board's own period (ADR 0102) and window every one of the nine counters on when the order arrived, so a badge and the tab beneath it count exactly the same orders; `period` (default ALL_TIME, which is what this endpoint answered before either parameter existed) instead cuts only completed, cancelled and total to the tenant's own business day (ADR 0043) — completed/cancelled on when the order closed, total on when it arrived — never to UTC midnight, and leaves the six live counters uncut: an order placed before the boundary and still in the kitchen is still in the kitchen. Supplying `from`/`to` together with a `period` other than ALL_TIME is refused with 400 INVALID_REQUEST rather than guessed at. The two mixes are exact server-side aggregates over the in-progress orders and sum to totalNonTerminal, regardless of which of the two periods was used.

post.description: orders.md §5.3. A POST with the number in the body, never a query string, resolving through the ADR 0015 keyed hash — never a LIKE over plaintext. Zero, one or several results are all ordinary: the hash index is deliberately not unique, because a household shares a phone and a recycled number changes owner. Picking a result is a selection, never a merge. Every call is a SECURITY-class ADR 0027 audit fact, matched or not, because this screen is a PII surface pointed at the tenant's entire customer base. No match: create the account with POST .../tenants/{tenantId}/customers, then place the order for it.

post.description: ADR 0145: a dispatcher-scope read with an ADR 0027 audited purpose, never a reporting fact -- a point is a doorstep, and a doorstep lives only inside the order's encrypted snapshot (ADR 0029). Opens the delivery orders of the tenant's current business day (ADR 0043) at this branch, newest first, at most 500. One audit fact for the whole call, written before any decryption, naming who, why and how many -- and not where. The answer carries an order number, a status, a time and a point, and nothing that identifies a person: no name, no phone, no address text. `withoutPoint` counts delivery orders with no point to show so a map never silently under-reports; `truncated` says the day held more than the cap. A purpose is required.
post.summary: Open today's delivery orders of this branch as map points (7.10a, 3.1)

get.description: The options behind the board's «Агрегатор» filter (orders.md §2.4, ADR 0040): one entry per provider binding that has an order at this branch, most recently used first, with how many and — where integration still resolves it — the provider and the installation's own name. Pass an entry's `bindingId` back as `marketplaceBindingId` on `GET .../orders/board`.
get.summary: The aggregator bindings this branch's orders arrived through

get.description: The one actor view this build can answer honestly: self-scoped by the token's own subject, never by a request parameter. `actorId` exists only so a caller can state its own subject back and be understood — passing any other value is refused with 403 INSUFFICIENT_CAPABILITY rather than answered with an empty or a substituted result, because `ORDER_READ` at this scope, however wide the grant, never authorizes reading another operator's own statistics; there is no staff directory yet to say whose they even are (the staff-identity ADR, IA `0.2c`/`0.2d`). Cut to the tenant's own business day (ADR 0043), the same boundary the live board's counters use.
get.summary: IA 0.2a: the caller's own orders today, by sales channel

post.description: Gap map row 1.3e. The same body as `POST .../orders`, run through the same cart and the same PricingEngine path that Создать takes, and then undone: the answer is the subtotal, the promotion discount, the delivery fee, the tax and the total the order would be booked at, with the amount of each line, so the New order screen can show the discounted price before it is placed. Nothing is written -- no cart, no stored quote, no redemption, no audit fact -- and nothing is reserved, so typing a promo code to see what it is worth does not use one up. A rule the cart would refuse on (an item out of stock, a promo code that does not apply, an address outside every zone) is refused here with the same code. The branch-override, pre-order and table fields of the body are accepted and ignored: they decide where and when an order is placed, not what it costs. A POST because the basket is a body; `ORDER_PLACE` because the answer is a price for a customer's would-be order. Needs an `Idempotency-Key`, which the screen mints fresh on every call.
post.summary: Price an order without placing it

post.description: The same body as `POST .../orders` and `POST .../orders/quote`, priced by the same path and then undone, and the answer is what the identified customer could redeem against the figure the order would be booked at: their spendable points, the largest redemption the brand's rules permit, why it is zero when it is, and the cash the customer would still owe for the redemption in redeemFromBalanceMinor (null when that is not an amount the offer permits, with requestedRefusal saying so). Nothing is written and nothing is held. The points are spent by sending redeemFromBalanceMinor and operatorAttestsCustomerAgreement: true with `POST .../orders`, inside its transaction, and never after the order exists (ADR 0185). A POST because the basket is a body; `ORDER_PLACE` because the answer is a figure for a customer's would-be order. Needs an `Idempotency-Key`, which the screen mints fresh on every call.
post.summary: What the customer may spend of their points on the order being taken

get.description: Platform-owned reference data (V0119), not a tenant registry: the same eight reasons for every tenant, read with ORDER_READ because the reject dialog has to populate its picker for every operator who can reject an order. `labels` carries every locale at once so the client renders whichever one the operator is using without a second round trip.
get.summary: The curated list a reject dialog picks from

get.description: Revision-aware (ADR 0039). The default is the order's current revision; naming an earlier one re-renders the lines as they were. A read that forgets to pin a revision double-counts, and the mistake stays invisible until somebody reconciles a total by hand.
get.summary: One order with its snapshotted lines

get.description: orders.md §3.6/§3.10's history view -- AmendmentResponse.commandDetails is what a courier or internal note's own text reads back through (OrderAmendmentService#noteOf); amend/confirmAmendment populate the same field with an empty list, since neither answers with an existing amendment's full command history.
get.summary: Every amendment on this order, applied or not

post.description: An amendment is not an edit. Applying one appends a revision carrying its own complete total and leaves the previous one byte-identical; it never rewrites a revision and never creates a second order. All twelve of ADR 0039's commands are built. REMOVE_LINES and a CHANGE_LINE_QUANTITY that lowers the quantity (ADR 0169) take a line off a confirmed order for a removal reason the tenant authored (removalReasonId, kind LINE_REMOVAL); the reason decides whether the stock goes back on the shelf or is written off, the kitchen's own record can only make that more conservative, and the response's stockConsequence says which before anything is applied. They are behind the brand's ordering.amendment_line_removal_enabled gate, need the customer's recorded agreement, and are refused on an order paid through a provider (PAID_ORDER_DECREASE_NOT_SUPPORTED).
post.summary: Amend a live order, appending a new revision

delete.description: The row stays, marked REJECTED. It is evidence of what an operator tried, and deleting it would make the attempt invisible to the next person asked why an order looks the way it does.
delete.summary: Withdraw an open amendment

post.description: The operator attests it on the call, and the attestation carries who, when, and through which channel. An amendment that raises the total cannot commit without one: charging more than the customer agreed to is the failure this prevents, and the database refuses the applied row as well. Wave 10: once attested, this also applies the amendment in the same call — the confirmation step closing the loop propose's own applyImmediately could not, because the total was not yet agreed. If something else still blocks it (an ADR 0027 approval, the POS export), the response is the amendment's current state, not an error: the confirmation itself always still succeeded.
post.summary: Record that the customer agreed to the change, and apply it

post.description: The first valid command wins under compare-and-set. A command that loses is recorded and inert, and the response reports the outcome that actually settled the order — so a second click gives the same answer as the first rather than an error. A rejection names a code from GET .../reject-reasons; OTHER additionally needs `note`.
post.summary: Approve or reject an order awaiting a decision

post.description: ADR 0064: a phone order is an ordinary operations order, and the only channel-specific fact about it is the call id its screen-pop card carried. Write-once — a second call with the same id is a harmless retry, and a second call with a different id is refused rather than silently overwriting where the order came from.
post.summary: Record the call this order originated from

post.description: With a reason from the tenant's registry (ADR 0039) this is permitted after confirmation: the reason names the stock disposition and the liable party, which is exactly what ADR 0019 refused to guess at. Without one it is still refused once confirmed, because none of those consequences has a default that is safe to assume. The operator never picks the write-off: the dialog shows what the reason carries and cannot change it.
post.summary: Cancel an order, recording why and what it cost

post.description: «Самовывоз выполнен» and «Доставлен сторонней службой» are different facts, and both the courier SLA report and the external-logistics settlement are built on the distinction. The reason is validated against the order's fulfilment mode; omitting it records the one the mode implies, because a dialog confirmed three hundred times a shift teaches people to click through dialogs.
post.summary: Complete an order, naming how it was completed

get.description: orders.md §3.8: дом, квартира, подъезд, этаж and ориентир, decrypted together with the coordinate that travels inside the same document. The detail screen shows only whether an address is on file; this is the capability-gated, audited call that opens it.
get.summary: Reveal the delivery address and instructions in full

get.description: orders.md §1.5: the detail screen shows the phone masked with no gate; going from masked to whole is this separate, audited call, mirroring GET .../lines/{lineId}/note. Copy-to-clipboard of the phone counts as a reveal and performs this call rather than copying an already-decrypted value.
get.summary: Reveal the customer's phone in full

get.description: At most one row is ever effective; every other row here is a click that lost the compare-and-set, a duplicate, or arrived after the order was already decided.
get.summary: Every decision this order ever received, including a losing one

put.description: ADR 0137. Writes the line's actual weight and corrects the line, the order's totals and, for an order still to be paid at the door, the amount it will collect: the same 'captured late, reconciled before the receipt is final' shape ADR 0038 gave marking codes. The weight is the whole line's, all its units together. Appends an order revision (source CATCHWEIGHT) carrying the signed delta. An order whose payment already runs through a provider is refused when the weight moves its total (PAYMENT_ALREADY_TAKEN) -- an increase or a refund is a provider operation this build does not perform. Until every weighed line of an order is reconciled the order cannot leave the pass (CATCHWEIGHT_NOT_RECONCILED). Capability order.advance: the same hands that hand the food over.
put.summary: Capture the weighed total of a catchweight line at pick or handover

post.description: ADR 0161. Records one marking code (a DataMatrix, scanned at the pass) against a line of an order that is CONFIRMED, PREPARING or READY. The server derives the stage (PICK or HANDOVER) from the status, normalises the code the way the console does, checks the structure per fiscal.marking.structure_check, checks the GTIN against the product's barcode when it has one, and refuses a unit that is already scanned anywhere in the tenant. The response carries the product identifier and the counts, never the code. Takes the order row's lock first, so a scan, a removal and a hand-over serialise. Replaying the same Idempotency-Key returns the first answer. Answers FEATURE_DISABLED (404-shaped) until feature.marked_goods is on for the tenant, and 429 with Retry-After beyond 240 scans a minute per principal.
post.summary: Capture one scanned unit of a marked order line

post.description: ADR 0161. Releases -- never deletes -- one scanned unit, with a coded reason (MISSCAN, UNIT_REPLACED, UNIT_DAMAGED) and no free text, while the order is still CONFIRMED, PREPARING or READY; refused as ORDER_NOT_MARKABLE once it has left the pass. Takes the same order-row lock as a scan and a hand-over and reads the status after it. A damaged symbol is answered by scanning another unit, or the order does not leave the pass: this is the way to take a wrong scan back, not a bypass.
post.summary: Take one scanned unit back

get.description: Separate from reading the order and requiring a stated purpose, because the note is the customer's own words about themselves (ADR 0029). A kitchen ticket needs it; an order list does not.
get.summary: Reveal one line's customer note

get.description: ADR 0161. Per marked line: the units required, the units captured, and each captured unit as its sequence, product identifier (GTIN), stage, time and the staff subject that scanned it. Never a code.
get.summary: The marked lines of an order and the units scanned against them

post.description: documentType is KITCHEN_TICKET, ORDER_SLIP or FISCAL_RECEIPT. A reprint is a new job, regenerated from the current facts, marked as a copy, linked to the first and recorded with the person and the reason. printerId chooses the printer; without it the document goes where its route says, and a document with no route is refused (NO_ROUTE). A fiscal receipt prints only for an ISSUED SALE document, and the refusal names the state. A kitchen ticket makes one job per station with items.
post.summary: Print an order's document again

get.description: At most twenty findings. Each says which promotions would give a different amount if the order were priced again at the checkpoint, and the totals either side. The order itself is unchanged by any of them.
get.summary: What the checkpoint found about this scheduled order's promotions, newest first

post.description: Prices the order's live basket again at this moment, under everything else it was bought with, and records how the promotions and the total differ. Writes no change to the order. Refused for an order that is not scheduled, is priced by an aggregator, or has already gone to its kitchen.
post.summary: Re-check a scheduled order's promotions now

get.description: Revision 1 is the ADR 0019 checkout snapshot and is byte-identical for ever. Each applied amendment appends one carrying a complete recomputed total plus the delta against its predecessor — the figure the operator read to the customer.
get.summary: Every revision of this order, with its own reproducible total

post.description: Guarded by the canonical state machine, including the fulfilment-mode split at READY: a pickup order cannot enter FULFILLING, where it would wait for a courier that does not exist.
post.summary: Move a confirmed order along the kitchen path

post.description: Not a literal reversal: OrderStateMachine declares each compensating edge as its own forward step, gated on ORDER_STATE_OVERRIDE rather than ORDER_ADVANCE and carrying a mandatory reason from the tenant's registry, its own timeline entry and its own audit fact. Refused for any target that is not a declared compensating edge, including every terminal order — a correction is never a reopening.
post.summary: Force a compensating transition that restores an earlier status

get.description: The answer to "why is this order in this state". An order row alone holds only the current status and can never answer it.
get.summary: Every transition, with what caused it and who

get.description: Device principals of class PRINT_AGENT, active and revoked alike, the printers each advertises (alias and last status) and the printer rows bound to it.
get.summary: The branch's print agents

get.description: The class the device asked for, shown to the approver before approving. An unknown, spent or expired code is the same 404.
get.summary: What a pending code claims

post.description: The userCode is read off the agent's own screen or log. The agent is granted exactly print.job.claim and print.job.report at this branch, never more; a code that asked to be anything else is refused 400 with nothing written. Writes an ADR 0027 security fact naming this manager and the device.
post.summary: Approve a pending print agent

post.description: Its grant is revoked first, cache-evicted at once, so the agent is refused on its very next request whatever its token's remaining life. A second press on a revoked agent is not an error.
post.summary: Revoke a print agent

post.description: Says which printers the agent can reach, by the alias it chose locally, and what each last reported (ONLINE, OFFLINE, OUT_OF_PAPER, COVER_OPEN, ERROR, UNKNOWN); a printer that reports anything but ONLINE stops being claimed from. Long-polls up to waitSeconds (at most 20). The reply first repeats this agent's own unexpired leases, so a retry after a lost reply returns what was claimed, and then claims the oldest claimable job of each idle printer, one at a time per printer in the order they were queued. A reply holds identifiers and 60-second lease tokens, never the paper. Requires an Idempotency-Key.
post.summary: Claim print jobs

post.description: A PNG of the same 1-bit bitmap the browser prints and an agent receives as raster, for a stored job (jobId) or for a document built the way a job would be (documentType and orderId, optionally stationId, printerId or tapeWidthMm). A POST because it carries a body; it changes nothing, so it declares its capability and needs no Idempotency-Key, and it reveals a line note only as the ticket prints it.
post.summary: The picture of what a job would print

get.description: Newest first, optionally one state (QUEUED, CLAIMED, PRINTED, HANDED_OFF, DEAD, CANCELLED, EXPIRED). The stored document is never returned: a list needs identifiers and outcomes, not the paper.
get.summary: The print queue

get.description: Its state, attempts and failure, never its document.
get.summary: One print job

get.description: The ESC/POS for the bound printer's width, rendered now from the stored document. Readable only with the job's live lease token (the lease query parameter) and only by the agent that holds it: a stale, expired or foreign lease is 409 and nothing is drawn. A document that cannot be drawn is 422 RENDER_FAILED and the job is dead.
get.summary: The bytes of a claimed job

post.description: Only a queued one: a claimed job is already on its way to paper (422 otherwise).
post.summary: Cancel a queued job

get.description: The workstation prints the preview bitmap through the browser (ADR 0154, Decision 10), so the person who asked for paper on a browser printer fetches the picture here: the same 1-bit bitmap the preview draws, for a job in state HANDED_OFF that this caller requested. A job that is anyone else's, is not handed off, or does not exist answers 404. It changes nothing. It declares print.reprint, the capability that made the job, because the preview's print.read -- a picture of any document of the branch -- is held by managers and not by the floor.
get.summary: The picture of a job the caller handed to the browser

post.description: For a dead, expired, cancelled or printed job: a new job, regenerated from the facts as they are now, marked as a copy, linked to the first print and recorded with the person and the reason. printerId chooses the printer; without it the document goes to the printer the old job was for, which must still be active. A job still queued or claimed, and a test page, are refused 422; a fiscal receipt is refused naming the state if its document is no longer an ISSUED SALE.
post.summary: Print a finished job's document again

post.description: PRINTED ends the job. FAILED, with a failureCode (PRINTER_OFFLINE, OUT_OF_PAPER, COVER_OPEN, TRANSPORT, RENDER), returns it to the queue after a backoff (5 s, 15 s, 45 s, 2 min, 5 min) or ends it DEAD on the sixth attempt. A stale or foreign lease token is 409 and changes nothing; the same PRINTED repeated is recognised and answered 200 REPLAYED. Requires an Idempotency-Key.
post.summary: Report what happened to a claimed job

get.description: True when the branch has an active binding that provides ORDER_EXPORT. The platform cannot read whether the till prints what it receives, so the routes screen says "your point of sale may already print this" beside the kitchen-ticket route. A statement: it creates, removes and refuses nothing.
get.summary: Whether the branch's point of sale may already print

get.description: Active and retired, with the roll, how each is reached and what its agent last reported. Never an address: the platform cannot make a branch machine dial one.
get.summary: The branch's printers

post.description: An agent printer names the agent (agentDeviceId) and the alias that agent advertises (agentPrinterKey); a browser printer names neither. A roll is 58 or 80 mm. Refused 422 PRINTING_OFF while feature.printing is off for the tenant.
post.summary: Register a printer

put.description: The version the form was opened at is If-Match; a second manager's save in between is STALE_VERSION. status RETIRED retires the printer: its routes stop printing and its jobs stay.
put.summary: Change or retire a printer

post.description: The roll's width, a ruler, every glyph the three languages use, a QR and the printer's name. A browser printer's job is recorded HANDED_OFF and its bitmap is the preview; an agent printer's is queued like any other.
post.summary: Print a test page

get.description: (Document type, optional station) to printer, with copies and auto_print. A branch with no routes prints nothing.
get.summary: What prints where at the branch

post.description: A station applies to a KITCHEN_TICKET only; a ticket for a station with no route of its own goes to the route with no station. autoPrint needs an agent printer.
post.summary: Create a route

delete.description: Under If-Match. Jobs already made from it stay.
delete.summary: Delete a route

put.description: Under If-Match. A route's document type does not change.
put.summary: Change a route

get.description: Every status in range, not only the ones holding a table: a host reading tonight's plan needs the cancellation next to the confirmed booking it replaced. No guest name, phone or note, the same restraint the single-booking read below keeps.
get.summary: A branch's bookings for a window — the day plan

post.description: One transaction for the whole party: a booking for four tables that can hold three holds none. A booking for a guest with no account creates no customer record and no consent (ADR 0015); the name and number are encrypted onto the booking itself.
post.summary: Take a booking

get.description: Omit `purpose` for the plain booking — no name, phone or note. Name one ("matching a walk-in", say) and the three fields decrypt, recorded as an ADR 0027 audit fact against that purpose. The audited reveal, not a second endpoint, is what a host stand actually needs.
get.summary: One booking, with the guest's details behind a stated purpose

post.description: `guestName`/`guestPhone`/`note` are optional — blank or omitted leaves whatever the booking already has. A host moving a table or a time has no need to re-type a number; one correcting a mistyped name or number now can, instead of only cancelling and rebooking. Refused once the booking is SEATED or terminal.
post.summary: Change the party size, the time, the tables, or the guest's own details of a booking not yet seated

post.description: Confirmation is where the hold is taken, and where a second host booking the same table for an overlapping time is refused by the database with a stable conflict code. Seating is not here: it opens a session, and lives on the session endpoint.
post.summary: Confirm, reject, cancel, or mark a booking as a no-show

post.description: The same self-service code as the tenant-scope route, for a brand or branch member: name the branch you work at and the capability is checked there. A location grant covers only its own branch, so naming another branch is refused; a brand or tenant grant covers the branches beneath it. The code always binds the caller's own account, whatever branch is named.
post.summary: Issue a staff Telegram identity-link code from a branch

get.description: Advisory, and honestly so. Two hosts reading this in the same second both see a free table; the database decides between them when they confirm. A screen that treated this as a hold would be the check-on-read ADR 0047 rejects.
get.summary: Which tables are free for a window, and which are occupied now

post.description: Ends this device's session. Idempotent: locking a terminal that is already locked is 204.
post.summary: Lock this terminal

post.description: A person with no PIN, or a locked one, types the code they were given and a new PIN. The code is single-use, expires, and is burned at the fifth wrong try; the PIN is refused with the reason stated when it is a run, a repeated digit, a common value or the last digits of the person's own phone or employee number (the code stays good). Success opens a session, as an unlock does.
post.summary: Set a PIN with a single-use activation code

post.description: Needs this device's live session (X-Terminal-Session) and the current PIN, which is checked under the same lockout as an unlock. The new PIN is refused with the reason stated under the same rules as an activation.
post.summary: Change the PIN of the person unlocked here

get.description: The people eligible at this terminal's location -- an active staff member holding every capability the class names for attribution -- as the labels the tenant chose (first name and the initial of the last, or the non-personal reference), each with whether they have a PIN. Never a phone, photo, employee number or subject. Empty while the device is DEVICE_ONLY. Cache-Control: no-store.
get.summary: Who may unlock this terminal

post.description: The keypad's tap that is not itself a mutating call (opening a ticket, scrolling the board) moves the idle deadline. 204, no body. No Idempotency-Key: its only effect is a timestamp moved forward, so a repeat is identical. The board's timed refresh never calls this.
post.summary: Keep this terminal unlocked

post.description: Opens the one live session of this device for the person who tapped their name and typed a PIN, ending the person's session elsewhere and the device's previous one. The token is returned once and is accepted only with this device's own bearer. A wrong PIN, an unknown member, an ineligible person and a person with no PIN all answer TERMINAL_UNLOCK_REFUSED alike; only a lock is distinguished (TERMINAL_PIN_LOCKED, with retryAfterSeconds when it will lift). No Idempotency-Key: the response carries a bearer.
post.summary: Unlock the terminal as a person

get.description: Of any class: name, class, state, attribution mode, the device's auto-lock and what applies now, who is unlocked at it, when it was last seen and the build it reported, who enrolled it and who revoked it. «Last seen» is the last authenticated request from the device, stamped at most once a minute: no heartbeat endpoint exists, so a healthy idle device and a stuck one are told apart by how long since.
get.summary: Every device at this branch

put.description: The version the form was opened at is If-Match; a second manager's save in between is STALE_VERSION. A mode other than DEVICE_ONLY is refused for a class nobody unlocks (422), and setting a device back to DEVICE_ONLY ends its sessions at once -- rollback restores today's attribution. autoLockSeconds null follows the tenant's policy; otherwise 30 to 3,600.
put.summary: Rename a device, set its attribution mode and auto-lock

post.description: Its grant is revoked first, so the next request is refused whatever its token's remaining validity; its Keycloak client is disabled and its terminal sessions end. A second press on a revoked device is not an error.
post.summary: Revoke a device

get.description: Newest first, twenty-five to a page, opaque cursor. The label is the one the tenant chose for a shared screen; the non-personal reference rides beside it.
get.summary: Who was unlocked at this device, when, and how it ended

get.description: Each carries url, the link as it is shared, built on the server from the brand's verified storefront hostname, the bot's username and the Mini App's short name; or unavailable, naming what is missing, and never both (ADR 0183).
get.summary: Every acquisition link this brand has minted, newest first

post.description: A website ?ref={token} link or a Telegram startapp deep link, for a campaign or an influencer. The token is opaque and short — a Telegram start deep link payload is limited to 64 URL-safe characters (ADR 0044).
post.summary: Mint a trackable acquisition link
Retire a link — it stops being minted new clicks against, and its history stays

get.summary: Every audience the brand has defined, newest first

post.description: A named, versioned predicate set from the closed catalogue — never a query. Gated the same as authoring a campaign, because targeting is part of composing one (ADR 0044 declares no separate authoring capability for audiences). An empty predicate list is refused: an audience with none is every customer of the brand, and that must be asked for rather than defaulted to by leaving a form empty.
post.summary: Define an audience

post.description: Metrics and account ids only. No contact value crosses this endpoint and none can. The export is itself an audited fact carrying the requester, the audience version, the row count, and the stated purpose, because an unrestricted download of the customer base is how a tenant's list ends up on a competitor's desk. Nothing here uploads a segment to a third party: that is a disclosure to a new controller, not a feature.
post.summary: Export a snapshot's members as pseudonymous account ids

get.summary: One audience with the predicates its current definition version holds

put.description: Never an edit of the old predicates — the definition version bumps, and every snapshot already built against the old version keeps meaning what it meant when it was built.
put.summary: Replace an audience's predicate set

post.description: Applies the predicates, then subtracts lifecycle, consent, suppression, frequency cap, and endpoint, recording the reason per exclusion. The member count is an upper bound: the same five checks run again per recipient at send, so the delivered count is always lower.
post.summary: Evaluate an audience into an immutable snapshot

get.description: q-rule-list's own priority order (X.25's first live consumer): lowest priority first, ties broken by name.
get.summary: Every automation rule this brand has authored

post.description: Written inert: active defaults to false at the schema, and only activation (a separate, campaign.approve-gated act) arms it. "Nothing sends without a human" is this split, not a checkbox on this form.
post.summary: Author an automation rule

put.description: q-rule-list's own whole-set contract: every id the caller means to keep, in the order it now wants, the same shape order-outcome-reasons' own reorder endpoint gives its sibling screen.
put.summary: Rewrite priority for the whole list

put.description: Refused while the rule is active: a marketer deactivates a running automation before changing what it fires, the same "stop, then change" posture a running campaign takes.
put.summary: Rewrite an inactive rule

post.description: The one act that lets this rule fire unattended. Gated by campaign.approve, the same second signature a campaign's own launch takes.
post.summary: Arm the rule

post.description: Reversible: reactivating asks for a fresh If-Match, not a fresh design.
post.summary: Stop the rule from firing

get.description: A bounded, tenant-scoped sample with the display name masked the same way OperatorCustomerLookupService masks one — never a real send, never a guard claim: AutomationRulePreviewService reuses the same candidate query a live firing would, but writes nothing.
get.summary: Which customers this rule would match today (row X.25)

get.description: Fired, refused (with its reason), or cancelled (the customer ordered before the send) — the same per-recipient honesty a campaign's own recipient list gives, at automation scale.
get.summary: This rule's recent firing history
Every campaign the brand has drafted, sent, or stopped, newest first

post.description: References an audience, a channel, and an ADR 0020 template key. Nothing here defines a discount or mints points: the campaign editor selects from an existing ADR 0018 offer or ADR 0046 accrual rule and has no field in which to invent one. DRAFT until estimated, submitted, and approved — nothing here sends anything.
post.summary: Draft a campaign

get.description: The list a marketer compares campaigns by (row 7.9b, ADR 0182): for each of the brand's hundred newest campaigns, the same `delivery` object `recipients/counts` answers for one, derived when asked from the messages' own evidence. One read so a screen does not ask a hundred times; a campaign that created no messages counts zero.
get.summary: What became of the messages of each of the brand's recent campaigns, side by side

get.description: Everything the detail screen renders honestly from: the four-eyes state (createdBy/approvedBy), the estimate as a range and not a promise, the reserved/spent split, and blockedCount/pausedAt for a paused send.
get.summary: One campaign's full lifecycle state

get.description: Every entry, reason and lift reason revealed together, in one audit fact. Requires a stated purpose.
get.summary: The decrypted blacklist history

post.description: Reason, actor, and an optional expiry (frontend information architecture §5.2). Refused while an entry is already active — lift it first. The enforcement point is CustomerIdentityService#resolve; see its own doc.
post.summary: Blacklist this customer
Lift the active blacklist entry

get.description: No reason, no reveal, no audit fact — mirrors CustomerProfileService's own existence-without-reveal split for contact points. Enough for the detail pane's badge; GET .../blacklist-entries is the reveal.
get.summary: Whether this customer is blacklisted right now, with no reveal

get.description: The guest's status, whether she is blacklisted right now, her leads, and a history merged by time from the messages sent to her, the campaigns that reached her, the promotions she redeemed, the reviews she left and the calls an operator made or took -- each owned and read from the module that holds it. Writes one audit fact per call. `before` and `beforeId` page further back: pass the previous page's nextBefore and nextBeforeId together, so entries that share the last one's instant are not lost. `before` alone means strictly older.
get.summary: Open one guest's card

get.description: What a subject-access request produces.
get.summary: The full consent history

post.description: Append-only. A withdrawal supersedes a grant without erasing it, because proving what someone agreed to and when is the obligation.
post.summary: Record a consent decision

get.description: Against the account itself and against any lead linked to it. Ids, codes and instants only. `before` and `beforeId` page further back from the last row of the previous page; `before` alone means strictly older.
get.summary: Every voice contact about this guest, newest first

post.description: Append-only, as a lead's. The brand is the brand's own line the call came in on or went out from, named in the body because an account is the tenant's.
post.summary: Record a call with a guest who is already an account

get.description: Requires a stated purpose, recorded as an audit fact.
get.summary: Reveal decrypted contact details

post.description: Accepts a value another account already holds. Refusing would be wrong: households share numbers, and merging on a match is what ADR 0015 forbids.
post.summary: Add a phone number or email address

delete.description: Tombstoned in place, never physically deleted — a delivery endpoint elsewhere may still reference this id. It stops counting anywhere: not in the profile's contact summaries, not in a reveal, and not as a verified endpoint for marketing eligibility.
delete.summary: Remove a contact point added by mistake

put.description: In place: the fix for a mistyped number, which used to be reachable only by adding a second, correct contact point and leaving the wrong one standing. The kind (phone or email) is not accepted here — it stays whatever this contact point already is. Verification resets: whatever proved the old value proves nothing about the new one.
put.summary: Correct a contact point's value

post.description: Demotes whichever contact point of the same kind held that place.
post.summary: Make this the account's primary contact of its kind

get.description: What was amended, against which evidence reference, by whom and when. The value that was replaced is kept but is not returned here: it is part of a data-subject export.
get.summary: The corrections made to this customer's data, newest first

put.description: Replaces the whole address, keeping the previous one under retention. Requires If-Match.
put.summary: Correct an address against evidence

put.description: The type stays; verification resets because the value changed. The previous value is kept under retention. `applied` is false when the value normalises to what was already there.
put.summary: Correct a contact point's value against evidence

put.description: Replaces a wrong date with the right one, keeping the previous date under retention. Clearing a date is not a correction. Requires If-Match.
put.summary: Correct the date of birth against evidence

put.description: The same edit as the profile PUT, with the previous name kept under retention and the evidence reference recorded. A blank name clears it. Requires If-Match. `applied` is false when the name was already that.
put.summary: Correct the display name against evidence

get.description: Requires a stated purpose, recorded as an audit fact.
get.summary: Reveal the date of birth

put.description: Staff-only, unlike the three self-service profile fields — CustomerProfileService#updateDateOfBirth explains why. A null `dateOfBirth` clears a value already on file. Requires If-Match.
put.summary: Set or clear the date of birth

get.description: A yes/no and, on no, one reason — CONSENT_WITHHELD or NO_VERIFIED_ENDPOINT. Never a contact value, so CUSTOMER_READ is enough; see CustomerEligibility's own doc for why this does not reuse marketing.MarketingEligibility.
get.summary: Whether this customer may be reached for a purpose and channel, right now

get.description: A legal hold, an order still on its way, a service-recovery case still open. Codes and counts only; empty when nothing stands in the way. Execute refuses with 422 UNPROCESSABLE_STATE naming the same blocks.
get.summary: What would stop this customer's erasure from executing right now

get.description: Whether a request is outstanding, was withdrawn, or already executed, and by whom.
get.summary: This customer's erasure-request history, newest first

post.description: Records intent; it does not erase anything by itself (ADR 0029, ADR 0044). Idempotent: a second call while one request is already PENDING returns that same request rather than raising a duplicate, and one for an already-anonymised account returns the request that anonymised it.
post.summary: Raise a data-subject erasure request on this customer's behalf

post.description: Idempotent for a request already CANCELLED. Refused for one that already COMPLETED — there is no undoing an erasure that already happened.
post.summary: Withdraw a PENDING erasure request

post.description: The transition that actually anonymises the account and overwrites its protected fields (ADR 0029) — deliberately a second, more tightly held capability than the one that raises a request. Idempotent: executing an already-COMPLETED request returns it unchanged rather than erasing twice.
post.summary: Execute an erasure request

get.description: The evidence ADR 0029 asks for: which participants ran and how many rows each overwrote or removed in each table, with when and by whom. Counts and table names only. 404 for a request that has not completed or that completed before proofs were kept.
get.summary: What an executed erasure changed, per module and table

get.description: Whether a request is waiting, produced, withdrawn or expired, and what the bundle contains by module and table (counts, never values).
get.summary: This customer's export requests, newest first

post.description: Records the request and the date the tenant owes an answer by; it gathers nothing by itself (ADR 0029). Idempotent: a second call while one is PENDING returns that same request.
post.summary: Ask for a copy of this customer's data on her behalf

get.description: The link works for a few minutes and is not stored. Each call is an audit fact naming you and your purpose, and appears in the merchant's egress log. 404 when the request has no bundle (not produced, expired, or removed by an erasure).
get.summary: A short-lived link to the produced bundle

post.description: Idempotent for a request already withdrawn. Refused for one already produced.
post.summary: Withdraw a PENDING export request

post.description: Reads her data from every module, decrypted under the purpose you state, into one JSON document that is kept for a limited time (ADR 0029). The purpose is recorded on the audit trail and appears in the merchant's egress log. Under an ADR 0027 approval when the tenant has published a customer.pii.export policy: the first call answers 422 SECOND_APPROVER_REQUIRED naming approvalRequestId, and once a second person has approved it the same call produces the bundle. Idempotent: a request already produced returns itself.
post.summary: Gather the customer's data into a bundle

get.summary: This customer's legal holds, newest first

post.description: While a hold stands, executing the customer's erasure is refused and the retention jobs that expire her data skip her (ADR 0029). Under an ADR 0027 approval: the first call answers 422 SECOND_APPROVER_REQUIRED naming approvalRequestId, and once a second person has approved it the same call places the hold. Idempotent: a customer who already has a hold gets that hold back.
post.summary: Place a legal hold on this customer

post.description: Releases the customer to an erasure request that was waiting behind the hold. Under an ADR 0027 approval, like placing one: the first call answers 422 SECOND_APPROVER_REQUIRED. Idempotent for a hold already lifted.
post.summary: Lift a legal hold

post.description: Identity merge for aggregator-masked identities (frontend information architecture §5.2): `accountId` becomes a redirect to `targetAccountId`, never the reverse — see CustomerIdentityService#merge for what this does and does not do. Requires If-Match against `accountId`'s own version.
post.summary: Merge this account into another

get.description: Only what has been set. An absent row means the default for that class, which is on rather than off: a customer who never expressed a preference has not opted out of anything.
get.summary: The customer's current preferences

put.description: Refuses a class the customer cannot switch off. Consent is separate and lives on the customers module; this never writes a consent decision.
put.summary: Set one preference

put.description: Requires If-Match, so a second tab loses loudly.
put.summary: Change the display name, language, or timezone

get.description: Reported as counts and two separate shares, never as one coverage figure. Cash is this market's majority tender and no payment provider can receipt it at all, so a single number would either report an unreceipted majority as healthy or a compliant restaurant as failing.
get.summary: How much of a window's trade has a provider receipt

get.description: Longest-waiting first. A blocked document is work with a reason, not an error: PROVIDER_REPORT_OVERDUE means a payment partner was asked and never answered, which on Payme's inbound-only reporting path is otherwise indistinguishable from a receipt that does not exist.
get.summary: Documents that owe a receipt and are waiting for a person

post.description: Reuses the document and never creates a second one: two sale receipts for one payment is a discrepancy with the tax authority that can only be corrected, never deleted. On the Click path the adapter reads back through GET payment/ofd_data first — a populated qrCodeURL means the earlier submission worked — because Click does not document submit_items as idempotent. The receipt lines are built from the order (ADR 0166): an order that cannot be built answers 200 with the outcome BLOCKED_CLASSIFICATION, BLOCKED_TAX, BLOCKED_RECONCILIATION or BLOCKED_MARKS, sends nothing, and the document carries the reason.
post.summary: Ask the partner for this document's receipt again

post.description: For the case where the thing blocking it is fixed — a classification entered, a terminal brought back. It asserts that the obstacle is gone, not that a receipt exists, so the document goes back to PENDING and its deadline is cleared rather than being marked resolved.
post.summary: Return a blocked document to the queue

get.description: A list, always. One order has several documents by design: a Payme PERFORM and its CANCEL are two receipts by the provider's own statement, and a split tender settles on two paths. A caller that expects one is reading a cancellation as though it replaced the sale.
get.summary: Every fiscal document for one order

post.description: The returned URL is signed for exactly this key, content type, and size, and expires shortly. Upload to it directly, then call finalize.
post.summary: Allocate an asset and return a constrained upload URL

get.summary: Read an asset's status

get.description: Only an AVAILABLE asset yields a URL; an unverified object is never served. Pass `variant` (THUMBNAIL/CARD/DETAIL) for a rendition rather than the original — a grid rendering dozens of images has no business fetching full-size originals for every one of them, and until this parameter existed there was no way to ask for anything else: every derivative ADR 0010's pipeline renders was stored and never served.
get.summary: Return a short-lived signed URL for a private asset

post.description: Never touches the object store. Records the client's claim that the upload finished and queues asynchronous verification; the returned status is UPLOADED, not AVAILABLE. A client's claim is not evidence, so nothing becomes displayable until a separate verification worker has read the object store's own metadata.
post.summary: Record that the upload is complete and queue verification

get.description: Including the ones that were never sent. A suppressed confirmation is the answer to the question that brought the operator here.
get.summary: Every message about one order, newest first

get.description: The provider's own wording is kept verbatim on each status, because 'accepted' and 'delivered to handset' are different promises and a support conversation turns on which one was actually given.
get.summary: One message, with its attempts and provider statuses

post.description: Re-runs the eligibility gate from the start, so consent withdrawn since cannot be overridden by pressing retry. A delivered message is refused: resending it is how a customer gets two confirmations from a well-meaning support action.
post.summary: Put a settled message back in the queue

get.description: Newest first. Usually one row; more than one names a genuine ambiguity -- the same number at two branches, or the same branch on two different days -- for the caller to resolve by branch or date, never by guessing the first.
get.summary: Every order at this tenant carrying this public order number

get.description: Never reads reporting.fact_order and is never read by it (ADR 0029's SubjectPseudonym exists precisely to stop that link). The customer's name renders in full and the phone masked, the same ordinary-read rule orders.md §1.5 states for the order board and detail screens — pass the same afterOccurredAt/afterOrderId pair GET .../reporting/orders's own response carries to page both reads together.
get.summary: Customer, operator and courier for orders in range — the console log's CRM half (7.2a)

post.description: Never reads reporting.fact_order (ADR 0029's SubjectPseudonym). The name renders in full and the phone masked, the same ordinary-read rule orders.md §1.5 states — identical decrypt path to GET .../orders/crm-log, batched by orderId instead of a date range because the board pages by cursor, not by time. An orderId absent from this tenant, or with no order at all, is simply missing from the response rather than refused.
post.summary: Customer name and masked phone for a batch of orders — the board's Клиент column (row 1.1)

get.description: Today is the tenant's own business day (ADR 0043), not the UTC calendar date. The two counts can both include the same order -- an operator who both created and approved it -- and are never added together server-side; see OperatorTodayCountsService's own doc.
get.summary: One operator's created/accepted order counts for today

get.description: Product analytics' q-abc-curve chart -- reporting.fact_order_line's own variant sales (the same source /variant-sales reads), sorted revenue-descending and walked into a running cumulative share, each row classed A/B/C against ClassificationThresholds.DEFAULT's published 80/95 split. Not the persisted classification-run (ADR 0134): that write is capability-gated and refuses a window under 28 days for its own XYZ half; this read has none and answers any range, never persisted.
get.summary: X.19: the ABC cumulative-revenue-share curve

get.description: Resolves a CANCELLED order's cancellationReasonCode (order_outcome_reasons.id, as a string) to the internal_name an operator actually picked, so the funnel's cancellation panel prints a name rather than a UUID. REJECTED/EXPIRED reason codes name a different, platform-fixed registry this does not cover.
get.summary: The tenant's cancellation-reason registry (7.1a)

post.description: Refused under a 28-day window (statistics.md S2.7): a Pareto over four days is an artefact of one large order, and the month preset is month-to-date, so the closest pill can silently be shorter than the floor -- this refuses rather than answering anyway. Always writes a new run, even over a window just computed: more orders may have closed since, and the run live when a class-C ruling was disputed is the one that defends it, not a cache that might now disagree.
post.summary: Compute and persist a new ABC/XYZ classification run

get.description: A read: seeing what was last computed never needs reporting.classification.run, only reporting.read. Answers RESOURCE_NOT_FOUND when nobody has run a classification over this exact window and location set yet -- the console offers a button to start one rather than treating an empty run as a rendering choice.
get.summary: The most recently computed run over this exact window, if any

get.description: One row per combo container over the closed business days in the range, straight off reporting.fact_order_line. A combo is sold as several ordinary lines that share a selection, and the container is never a line, so combosSold takes one quantity per purchase (distinct combo_selection_id) while the money is the sum over the purchase's component lines. Completed orders only: a combo on a cancelled or rejected order was not sold. A component sold on its own is not counted here, and the same dish sold as a component still appears in /variant-sales under its own name. maybeMore is true when the bounded read came back full.
get.summary: Sales by combo (ADR 0136): how many of each combo were sold, and for how much

get.description: Order amount vs charged delivery vs provider billed vs variance vs reconciliation status, off reporting.fact_external_delivery_cost (V0412, w6-reporting-facts batch 11) -- one row per PARTNER-sourced delivered shipment, projected at business-day close. reconciliationStatus is UNBILLED (never PENDING) for a shipment with no invoice line at all -- 'HorecaOS has a shipment the partner never billed', excluded from varianceMinor's own total the same way it is excluded from every sum here: a null variance never contributes. This is a close-time snapshot, not a live reconciliation state: a line matched or reconciled after its business day closed is not reflected here. The invoice-scoped half of this reconciliation renders in Finance 8.4; this is the per-order cut.
get.summary: 7.4c: per-order external-delivery cost

get.description: One row per courier across the range, straight off reporting.fact_delivery (ADR 0125). courierId only; resolve display through the couriers endpoint (P19), never from this report.
get.summary: 7.4: courier leaderboard — distance, transit hours, deliveries, on-time %

get.description: The COURIER scope of agg_sla_bucket_day (ck_agg_sla_scope_kind has allowed it since V0031; this is the first producer and reader). Same sla_bucket_set.v1 six buckets as the branch distribution, bucketed on a courier's own acceptance-to-delivery span rather than the order's full elapsed time.
get.summary: 7.4a: the fixed SLA distribution, per courier

get.description: reporting.fact_delivery_fee_resolution (V0411, w6-reporting-facts batch 11), one row per delivery_fee_resolutions row (ADR 0037) that named a tariff, joined at close time through quote -> order -> shipment for the one column none of the three tables has alone: which courier actually worked each resolution. Grouped by (tariff, courier), over the closed business days the range covers.
get.summary: 7.4b: delivery-sum-by-tariff audit

get.description: Every customer whose first-ever order fell inside [from, to], grouped by that order's calendar month, with the share of each cohort placing any order in every subsequent month through "to". Refuses a range covering more months than the read tracks in one call rather than silently truncating retention for the earliest cohorts.
get.summary: 7.6a: monthly cohorts by first-order month, and their retention curve

get.description: One folded figure per metric over the whole requested range — a KPI tile shows one number for its period, not a day-grain breakdown. Not /queries: a distinct-customer count cannot be correctly summed across the channel/fulfilment-type rows that pipeline rolls agg_branch_day up from. customers.ltv.v1 is not here — it is registered unbuilt (no dim_customer table exists) and every tile naming it must render that rather than a number.
get.summary: 7.6: new/distinct customers, repeat share, order frequency, customer value, basket depth

get.description: Platform-fixed bands, never tenant-configurable — the same rule sla_bucket_set.v1 already follows. Distinct from 5.3's segment builder: a marketer can size one segment there and read the whole grid here to decide which cell is worth targeting. Monetary is a cell value, not a third bucketed axis.
get.summary: 7.6b: the Recency x Frequency cross-tab, member counts and revenue per cell

get.description: delivery_distance.average.v1 — the mean of reporting.fact_order.delivery_distance_meters over delivery orders closed in range. Null when nothing in range resolved a distance, which is not a zero-metre delivery.
get.summary: Mean resolved delivery distance for the overview's distance tile (7.1)

get.description: delivery_transit_time.average.v1 — the branch leaderboard's own `Ср. время доставки` column for every branch at once, read from reporting.fact_delivery (ADR 0125). Courier-leg-only, from acceptance to delivery, never the door-to-door figure `delivery-time` answers. A branch with no settled delivery in range is simply absent from `rows`, never a row carrying a null average.
get.summary: Average courier transit seconds, per branch, in one query (7.3)

get.description: Wave W02. hourOfDay is operating-day-relative, matching demand-history. runId is null when ForecastScheduler has not generated a run for this location and weekday yet; hours is empty when the run exists but its sample was too thin to publish any hour (the same refusal demand-history makes). actualQuantity and absolutePercentageError are null on an hour until that business date's day closes.
get.summary: The seasonal-naive forecast for one location and weekday, with its confidence interval and comparison to what actually happened

get.description: dimension=CATEGORY groups by kitchen/menu category (department); dimension=VARIANT groups by product, capped to the best-selling products in the sample the run was generated from. No confidence interval at this grain in this wave — confidenceLow/confidenceHigh do not appear on these rows at all, unlike the branch-level demand-forecast.
get.summary: 7.8a: the latest forecast run's department or product breakdown

get.description: Not a forecast (the owner's 2026-09-05 decision, ADR 0043's implementation status): an average of completed orders in each hour, over the location's most recent occurrences of the requested weekday. hourOfDay is operating-day-relative (0 is the location's own business-day start), not wall-clock. Below minimumSampleSize qualifying dates, averageOrders is null on every hour and ordersByDate carries the raw per-date counts instead, so a sample too thin to mean anything is never shown as a confident number. holidayMode (7.8b) controls how a tenant.public_holidays date in the sample counts: INCLUDE (default) fully, EXCLUDE not at all, WEIGHT at half.
get.summary: Historical average order count by hour, for one location and weekday

get.description: Half-open intervals in meters, exhaustive and fixed per version. Read-only: the buckets are platform-fixed (row 7.10b's own doc) so a chart drawn under one version keeps its meaning.
get.summary: The delivery-distance buckets the histogram is computed in, and their version

get.description: distance_bucket_set.v1: six half-open meter intervals, exhaustive and non-overlapping, computed live over reporting.fact_delivery.distance_meters (not a nightly aggregate — see DistanceBucketSet's own doc). A bucket with no deliveries in range is a real zero, never a missing row.
get.summary: The fixed delivery-distance distribution, tenant/branch/period scoped (7.10b)

get.description: The export centre screen's own job history, newest first. A viewer who lacks customer.pii.export never sees another principal's PII columns or download URL in this list.
get.summary: Recent report exports

post.description: Excel/CSV as an audited PII egress (ADR 0043/ADR 0029). The PII column group (customer.pii.export) is included only when the requesting principal holds it -- otherwise it is silently omitted from the artefact rather than refusing the whole request. Processed asynchronously; poll GET .../reporting/reports/{id}.
post.summary: Queue a report export

get.description: delivery_time.median.v1 / pickup_time.median.v1 — the overview's pickup/delivery elapsed-time tiles. Null when nothing of that fulfilment type closed in range, which is not a zero-second delivery.
get.summary: Median seconds from order creation to close, for one fulfilment type (7.1)

get.description: The metric dictionary. A definition whose source fact is not built says so, and a definition finance has not signed is marked provisional rather than presented as settled.
get.summary: Every metric this build defines, with its definition and signature

get.description: One row per operator, human or machine: operator_principal_id is a staff Keycloak subject when a person created or accepted the order, or a pseudo-operator named after its channel ("channel:BOT", "channel:WEBSITE") otherwise, so the bot and the website compare against people rather than disappearing from the board. displayName (ADR 0139) is the tenant's own name for a staff row, composed here and never in reporting, and null for a pseudo-operator and for a subject the tenant keeps no name for; principalKind and subject still say what the row is.
get.summary: 7.5: orders taken, revenue, average check and handling time, per operator

get.description: Straight off fact_order_line joined back to fact_order for the operator who took it, on the same footing as /variant-sales. Pass an operatorPrincipalId straight off an /operator-leaderboard row.
get.summary: 7.5a: one operator's product mix, drilled down from the leaderboard

get.description: One grouped read behind two surfaces: sum by terminalStatus for the overview funnel's drop-offs, or read the CANCELLED/REJECTED/EXPIRED/PAYMENT_FAILED rows for the cancellation panel's reason breakdown. What a cancellation cost — stock_disposition, liability_party — is not here: ADR 0039's order_outcomes does not exist yet, so fact_order carries null on every row for both.
get.summary: Every terminal status in range, split by cancellation reason

get.description: Not day-grain: one row per order, straight off reporting.fact_order. Carries no name, phone, operator, or courier — reporting has no PERSONAL field at all (ADR 0029). A bounded read, ordered by the axis the requested sort names, not a paginated feed; maybeMore on the response says whether it came back full.
get.summary: Order-grain rows behind 7.2's per-stage, commercial-log, and late-order tables

get.description: payment_mix.amount.v1, over reporting.fact_order_tender: net tendered amount per payment method, from tenders that reached SETTLED or REVERSED. "overview" folds every branch into one row per method and legal entity (ADR 0038: never across two, since this is money); "byLocation" keeps the branch split so 7.3b's cash reconciliation can answer from the same read. legalEntityId narrows both to one taxpayer; paymentMethodCode narrows both to the named methods.
get.summary: Takings split by payment method — the cash-collection control figure (7.1c/7.3b)

get.description: Its own endpoint because a median cannot be composed from per-slice medians. Null when nothing reached READY in the range, which is not a zero-second kitchen.
get.summary: Median seconds from confirmation to ready

get.description: The branch leaderboard's own `Ср. время приготовления` column for every branch at once — replaces fanning out one `.../preparation-time` call per branch. A branch with no order that reached READY in range is simply absent from `rows`, never a row carrying a null median.
get.summary: Median seconds from confirmation to ready, per branch, in one query (7.3)

get.description: Newest first, at most 500 rows. Includes orders that were later cancelled, with their order status, so a count that excludes them can be reproduced.
get.summary: 7.9: the redemption log - one row per (order, promotion), customer as a pseudonym

get.description: One row per promotion and legal entity over the closed business days in the range (the promo.* metrics are money, and ADR 0038 refuses a total across two companies). Cancelled, rejected, expired and payment-failed orders are excluded here and stay in the log. A customer's one-off benefit grant has no promotion: its rows carry no promotionId and are labelled by where the grant came from. The average check with and without is a comparison over the same brand, entity and period, not a causal uplift: customers who use a promotion differ from those who do not.
get.summary: 7.9: promotion summary - redemptions, unique customers, discount given, average check with and without

get.description: Unknown metric ids are rejected rather than ignored: a silently dropped column renders as a quiet day. A money metric is refused unless the answer names the legal entity, because a combined total across two entities reconciles to neither tax filing (ADR 0038).
get.summary: Named metrics over a date range, grouped by named dimensions

get.description: What the export centre screen polls: QUEUED/RUNNING/COMPLETE/FAILED, the effective columns actually produced, whether the row quota truncated the result, and a short-lived download URL once COMPLETE. A viewer who lacks customer.pii.export never sees another principal's PII columns or download URL here, even for their own completed export.
get.summary: One report export's status

get.description: A case counts as opened on its opening business day and closed on its closing day, so the two counts and the two durations are over different sets. Means are whole seconds rounded to the nearest; the 90th percentile is continuous over the same set. The breach rate is in basis points. Remedy money is returned per currency as it was attached and is not a registered metric (recovery.remedy_money is declared unbuilt: ADR 0038 needs a legal entity the compensation link does not carry).
get.summary: recovery.*: service-recovery cases per location - opened, closed by outcome, times, breach rate

get.description: One row per location over the closed business days in the range. Every review counts, whatever became of its comment: a rating is not words. The average is the sum of ratings over the count, half up to one decimal, and is null when the range holds no review. Tags are counted by category and sentiment, never by wording.
get.summary: reviews.count, reviews.average_rating, reviews.tagged: reviews per location and the tags they carried

get.description: Half-open intervals in minutes, exhaustive and fixed per version. Read-only: ADR 0043 fixes the buckets platform-wide so a chart drawn under one version keeps its meaning; this tenant can read the definition, not edit it.
get.summary: The elapsed-time buckets orders are reported in, and their version

get.description: sla_bucket_set.v1: six half-open intervals that are exhaustive and do not overlap, so the shares sum to the whole. Not a tenant setting — an editable bucket rewrites every chart already drawn.
get.summary: The fixed elapsed-time distribution per branch

get.description: One row per product variant, summed over the range and split by delivery vs. pickup, straight off reporting.fact_order_line joined to its own order for the fulfilment type. Not a registry metric: the registry's one-value-per-slice contract does not express a per-product breakdown, the same reason order-grain reads get their own endpoint rather than folding into /queries. fulfilmentType narrows every column, including the totals: a DINE_IN order has no delivery or pickup column of its own, so the totals with no filter applied can exceed delivery plus pickup by exactly its share. sort (wave 10 w5-reports-exports, 7.7) is QUANTITY_DESC/REVENUE_DESC (default)/NAME_ASC; afterQuantity/afterRevenueSom/afterProductName plus afterVariantId page past the bounded read with a keyset cursor, matching whichever one field the requested sort names on the previous page's last row -- the other two are ignored.

get.description: ADR 0145 and ADR 0037: off reporting.fact_delivery_fee_resolution, the closed fact that carries the zone a fee was resolved against, so the density view needs a zone and never a coordinate. A zoneId of null is the deliveries no drawn zone covered -- priced by the branch's own tariff -- which is the figure that exposes a badly cut zone. Counted from fee resolutions that named a tariff, so a delivery priced outside the tariff model is not in it. Money is integer minor units, grouped by currency.
